result.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
result.summary: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. To address these issues, we propose Mixture-of-Features Attention (MoFA), a lightweight feature-encoding approach equipped with a working memory that encodes previously rejected proposals. Leveraging MoFA, rejection memory, and a set of further enhancements, including 2-tap causal convolutions, prefix-only cross-attention, and non-uniform target layer selection, the final architecture, DNeo, achieves 1.3x faster generation speed than SoTA (DFlash-2) without impacting drafter footprint or generation quality. DNeo marks a new state of the art in high quality, fast LLM inference.

AI.brief_summary: 针对推测式扩散解码中并行草稿模型对目标模型特征编码有损、无记忆、层采样均匀的问题，提出 MoFA 及拒绝记忆、因果卷积、前缀交叉注意力与非均匀层选择，构成 DNeo，在保持草稿模型规模与质量的同时加速生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本推理加速工作，但其「target 特征经投影有损（residual mixing）」「总拒绝提案的工作记忆」与「非均匀选取 target 层隐状态」三条线索，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 承载任务必要信息、被拒轨迹复用与跨层证据筛选的设计。
